newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares firm on surprise rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares firm on surprise rate cut.

text.p: The Oslo bourse crept higher on Tuesday, mainly buoyed by a surprise cut in interest rates by the central bank. Sentiment was positive for the industrial blue chips and the banking sector.
The Total share index lifted 0.5 percent to 878.50 points in healthy turnover of 707 million crowns.

The index lifted almost three points after the central bank announced it was trimming its overnight deposit rate to 4.0 percent from 4.50 percent and the overnight lending rate to 6.0 percent from 6.50 percent.
"I was negative to the market outlook before the rate cut, but now everything appears more positive," said one broker. "I'm surprise the market didn't go up even more."
Banks continued on an upward trend following positive third quarter results last week. The banking index climbed 1.26 percent to 82.99 points.

Diversified industrial group Kvaerner climbed nearly four percent, or 9.50 crowns, to 250.50 crowns on a positive analyst's recommendation and expectations of improved third-quarter results, due for release next Monday.
Kvaerner's B share rose 7.50 crowns to 229 crowns.
